sentence: This project studies how tissues communicate through endocrine interactions and how disease disrupts them, using computer methods and mouse models of metabolic disease.
This project studies the causes of cancer and tests ways to prevent it, detect it early and improve life after a cancer diagnosis.
This project builds imaging methods that measure blood flow in bone marrow of the knee using a very strong magnetic field.
This project builds a shared resource that uses CRISPR gene editing and microscopy to study how changes in genes affect cells.
This project studies how the protein tumor necrosis factor alpha drives chronic disc pain in the back, using rat and human model systems.
This project studies how the dopamine response of the brain to eating differs between weight groups and sexes, using very detailed brain imaging.
This project builds a way to find early cancer spread using a nanoparticle-based method and magnetic particle imaging.
This project looks for genomic changes in advanced prostate cancer that predict how the disease progresses and responds to treatments, by sequencing many tumor samples.
This project tries to improve CRISPR gene editing by evolving guide RNA scaffolds and using machine learning to predict the best ones.
This project builds a tool that collects gut microbiome data at large scale and a program that forecasts changes in microbes.
This project tests whether a drug that blocks glucosylceramide synthase can fight triple-negative breast cancer in mouse models and how it triggers an immune response.
This project studies whether heart muscle changes appear early as kidney function declines in people with type 1 diabetes.
This project builds a chip that models human bone marrow and its stem cell niche using hydrogel scaffolds and demineralized bone paper.
This project tests whether a gene therapy that uses epigenetics can treat a common inherited form of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia.
This project studies how the immune system can be restored so it clears cells infected with HIV.
This project adds equipment to a core facility that measures lipids and other small molecules in very small tissue samples.
This project studies how psilocybin-assisted therapy changes brain networks in patients with alcohol use disorder, including self-reflection and alcohol cue circuits.
This project studies how microRNAs help control the layout of liver functions, called metabolic zonation.
This project uses metabolic imaging to find out how cancer therapies damage the heart and to detect that damage earlier.
